issues.claim: "A name search lands on a GoDaddy parking page with a 'Get This Domain' button, so it can look as if the domain is up for grabs..." (audit_md, What it means for customers)
issues.problem: Unsupported assertion about search results. No SERP screenshot or citation is given, and nothing in the record shows the domain appearing for a name search. When I tried brand searches myself, the results I could reach returned directories and the Google listing (yellowpages, nextdoor, groomerjob, dogdog, bbb), not goochie-pooch.com; Google, DuckDuckGo and Bing SERPs were blocked or unusable from this network, so the claim can be neither confirmed nor refuted, only flagged as unsourced. The verified paths to the parking page are the Nextdoor site link and typing the old address, not a name search.
issues.fix: Replace with the paths that were actually verified, e.g. "Anyone who follows the website link on the salon's Nextdoor page, or types the old address, lands on a GoDaddy parking page with a 'Get This Domain' button, so it can look as if the domain is up for grabs." If a search-results claim is kept, add a dated SERP screenshot or citation for it.

issues.claim: "Hours differ: Nextdoor Mon-Fri 9-5, Google Friday 9-4, GroomerJob/dogdog.org Tue-Sat 9-4" and "hours disagree across Google, Nextdoor, GroomerJob and dogdog.org"
issues.problem: Each per-source figure is correct, but the framing overstates the disagreement. GroomerJob and dogdog.org list identical hours (Tue-Sat 9-4, Monday closed), so hours do not "disagree across" those two, and Google's Friday 9-4 matches them. The only hours conflict I could confirm is Nextdoor's Mon-Fri 9-5 against the 9-4 listings; Google's other six days were not visible in the limited Maps view, so a Google-vs-directory conflict on other days is unproven.
issues.fix: Name the single confirmed conflict: "Nextdoor says Mon-Fri 9-5; Google's Friday hours and the two grooming directories say 9-4, and the directories close on Monday." Drop "disagree across" phrasing.

issues.claim: "goochie-pooch.com, the domain the salon used until 2020"
issues.problem: Stated as fact, but the archive only shows the salon's own site captured on that domain from 2013-03-28 to 2020-11-30; nothing proves it was abandoned on that date (the record's own caveats say the parking start date cannot be established). Minor, but it is an inference presented flatly.
issues.fix: Say "the domain that carried the salon's old site, last archived in November 2020" or add "(as far as the Internet Archive shows)".

issues.problem: Counting the body text (headings excluded) comes to roughly 305-315 words, just over the brief's limit.
issues.fix: Trim about 15 words, e.g. shorten the customer-impact paragraph once issue 1 is fixed.
